title: Two Talmuds, one Mishnah
hookLine: the Jerusalem Talmud, from Galilee, and the Babylonian, built on the same Mishnah
carry: one Mishnah, two Talmuds, both kept

cards: Two families get the same recipe card from a grandmother. One stays in the old house, near the garden where the vegetables on the card actually grow. The other moves far away, to a big city with a busy market.

Years pass. Both keep cooking from the card, writing notes in the margins, arguing about the salt. One day the two notebooks are laid side by side: the same card at the center, very different notes around it.
That's roughly what happened to the Mishnah. Today's word is the notebook that stayed close to home.

teach.b: Yerushalmi. It's the name for the Jerusalem Talmud, sometimes called the Talmud of the land of Israel.
First, a surprise: despite the name, tradition places its sages not in Jerusalem but in the towns of Galilee, in the north of the land.
The other Talmud is the Bavli, the Babylonian Talmud, from the academies of Babylonia, far to the east. Both start from the same Mishnah, and both add a Gemara, the discussion, mostly in Aramaic.
Second, each shows where it was made.

teach.h: FARMING LAWS STAY IN THE LAND.
teach.b: The Yerushalmi discusses the Mishnah's farming laws: the gifts for the poor at the corners of a field, the tithes, the year the land rests. Those laws belong to the soil of the land of Israel, where its sages lived.
The Bavli, made far away, gives them much less room. Third, the feel.

teach.h: SHORTER AND HARDER, LONGER AND WORKED.
teach.b: Some readers who move between them describe the Yerushalmi as shorter and harder, its arguments left more in outline, while the Bavli's run longer and are worked over more.
The Talmud this path has been reading, with Rashi and Tosafot around it, is the Bavli. Fourth, the Bavli keeps a hard word about itself.
In tractate Sanhedrin, a sage reads a verse from Lamentations about being made to dwell in dark places, and says: that's the Talmud of Babylonia.
The Bavli prints that line on its own page, admitting its way of arguing can feel like walking in the dark.
Two Talmuds, one Mishnah, and a family that kept both notebooks.

how: In yeshivas the Babylonian Talmud is the usual text of daily learning, and the Jerusalem Talmud is also studied, especially for the agricultural laws of the land of Israel. Some study cycles move through the Yerushalmi page by page as well.

games.q: you're a sage reading a verse from Lamentations: he has made me dwell in dark places. in tractate Sanhedrin, what do you say it describes?
o: a cave where a prophet hid.
games.why: in tractate Sanhedrin, a sage applies the verse to the Babylonian Talmud, and the Bavli keeps that line on its own page.

practice: Say the Mishnah's very first question quietly to yourself: from what time may one recite the Shema in the evening?
Picture it read in a study house in Galilee, then in an academy in Babylonia: two rooms far apart, one question at the center. If you say the Shema, say its first line slowly, as both rooms did.
If you don't pray, sit with the picture of two rooms holding one page.
